utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I'm not aware of any preliminaries. Therefore, in order to hear the remainder of the testimony of the witness, I'd like to move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. May I take it that the Prosecution is ready to call its next witness after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would be mister?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: John Jordan. And the witness will be led by Mr. Adam Weber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weber, and there are no protective measures of any kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we take a break, and we resume at ten minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning. Adam Weber on behalf of the Prosecution. Yes, we are. At this time, the Prosecution seeks leave to present the evidence of John Jordan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May the witness be escorted into the courtroom. On the Defence side, will it be you, Mr. Ivetic, who is going to cross-examine the witness later?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, the Chamber was informed that from the list of associated exhibits you're going to use six. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, pursuant to Rule 92 ter, we're going to be tendering the statement of the witness and then five associated exhibits. At that time, I will be using associated exhibits but during the course of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jordan, I take it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I'd like to invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Jordan. Mr. Jordan, you will first be examined by Mr. Weber. You will find him on your right. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Weber, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could I invite you also, Mr. Jordan, to make a short pause between question and answer. Mr. Weber will show you how to make a pause between answer and question so that the interprets are able to follow you what you saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, could you please introduce yourself to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: My name is John Jordan. I'm from Garnet Lake, New York.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please display page 1 of 65 ter 28347. It's a statement of Mr. Jordan signed on the 24th of August, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, once the document is on the screen, if you could please look at it and verify whether or not your signature appears at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document, and that is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you review this statement prior to coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the lower portions of page 9 in the English and page 10 in the B/C/S. Sorry, it's actually the middle portion of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to paragraph 45, where you describe an incident involving two men in a building in Grbavica, are there any corrections you would like to make to this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yeah. One point I remembered it was actually surrey.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you have any additional clarifications or corrections to the statement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the last page of the statement in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, does your signature appear on this page?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were asked questions similar to those that you were asked during the taking of this statement, would you provide the same answers, in substance?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now that you have take the solemn declaration in this case, do you affirm the truthfulness and accuracy of this statement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders the 2006 statement uploaded under 65 ter 28347 into evidence as a public exhibit. The Prosecution also tenders at this time five associated exhibits. For the record, they are 65 ter 10064, 14090, 14096, 14097, and 65 ter 14108, all the associated exhibits are also being tendered as public exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On behalf of the Defence no objection to the introduction of the statement, and as I had indicated to Mr. Weber earlier today, no objection to these associated exhibits being introduced with the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the statement, the 2006 statement would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28347 becomes Exhibit P126, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Then we go to the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10064 becomes Exhibit P127, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14090 becomes Exhibit P128, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14096 becomes Exhibit P129, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14097 becomes Exhibit P130, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14097 becomes Exhibit P130.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P130 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And document 14108 becomes Exhibit P131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P131 is admitted into evidence. You may proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution seeks leave to present a public summary of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please present that summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: John Jordan was one of several international volunteer fire fighters in Sarajevo between 1992 and 1995. In 1992, the witness was a volunteer fire-fighter in the United States.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please slowdown for the transcription.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. He saw a news footage about the war in Sarajevo and started an organisation with his own funds to assist the local fire-fighters in Bosnia. This organisation was called Global Operation Fire Rescue Services, known also by the acronym GOFRS. Mr. Jordan arrived in Sarajevo in November 1992. The witness describes his observations and experiences in Sarajevo between November 1992 and September/October 1995. During this time, members of GOFRS worked alongside local Serb and Muslim fire-fighters and responded to fires on both sides of the confrontation lines. The vast majority of these fires were in the area controlled by the Bosnian government authorities. Mr. Jordan personally attended between 250 and 300 fires during the war in Sarajevo and assisted at least 200 civilians, the vast majority of whom were injured as -- the vast majority of whom were injured as a result of shelling and sniping attacks from Bosnian Serb forces. The witness observed that civilians were caught up in such attacks while going about their daily lives. Mr. Jordan describes incidents that took place in 1993 through 1995. The witness and members of his organisation came under attack on multiple occasions. Several of the fire-fighters from GOFRS were present and witnessed sniping incident F12. Mr. Jordan was informed of the circumstances related to the death of the victim in this incident along with the wounding of his mother. In light of the Trial Chamber's rulings on adjudicated facts, the Prosecution does not intend to lead evidence that has been covered extensively by adjudicated facts 1930 to 1932, 2018, 2045, 2047, 2053, and 2054, 2056, 2065, 2143, 2154, and 2159. That completes the public summary of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, in paragraph 2 of your statement which is now P126, you mention that you were part of the United States marine corps as a scout sniper. Could you please tell us what years you served as a marine?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: 1973, September, till August 1978.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution is now going to ask you to watch a series of video-clips from the DVD that you provided in 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which, for the record, Your Honours, is referenced on page 3, paragraph 12 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, after each clip, I will ask some questions for you to assist us with what is depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will now ask Ms. Stewart to please play 65 ter 22481A.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "Barely a day goes by without some part of Sarajevo bursting into flames. Morning and night, it doesn't matter when or where. There have been 300 major fires in five months. These are not accidents. This is arson on a massive scale, and there's a terrifying pattern to this pyromania. First Serbian shells fired from the surrounding hills set a building ablaze, then the gunners wait until the firemen arrive before launching another barrage. Anti-aircraft fire pounds into this towering inferno. The idea is keep the burnings blazing to burn as much of the city as possible. The firemen are not just fighting fires, they are always under fire. "An ambulance riddled with bullet-holes. In Sarajevo, even the men who try to save are targets. The fire brigade is having to rely on inexperienced young men to cope with an almost impossible task. The firemen are poorly equipped and undermanned. In the last six months they fought 300 major fires. In peacetime, a serious fire would happen around every five years. But Sarajevo burns every day. The men have no breathing apparatus, no protective clothing. They wear only their thin uniforms. The threat of snipers often prevents them from using mechanical lifts, but their long hoses have all worn out through constant use. Now hoses will only reach up to five stories of an apartment block. Anything above can't be --"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, there appears to be two separate news broadcasts in the clip that we just watched. Are these broadcasts similar to the ones you saw in 1992 before you went to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: They are, in fact, the ones I saw before I went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know the approximate date of each of these media reports?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I believe they were the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since you are speaking too quickly, especially also because what is heard on the video goes very quickly, you should -- after having shown the video, you should wait with your first question until the translation has been finished. So please take care, because both B/C/S and French booth had difficulties in following the speed of speech already before you started, and you didn't make it any better.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, of course. Thank you for the reminder. I will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Perhaps you -- in your first question I think has been recorded approximate date of each of these media reports, summer 1992. Resume from there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who these media reports were from?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The first report was provided to us by Christiane Amanpour of CNN. The second one, which depicts the ambulance, is from Tony Bartley who I believe was with ABC news at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to that ambulance that we saw with a number of holes in it, do you recognise this ambulance?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Whose ambulance is it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That ambulance was on the BiH side. It was often at the State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this video-clip there are individuals wearing yellow helmets who were attempting to extinguish firings. Who are these fire-fighters?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: They would be firemen from the Sarajevo fire department, BiH side. They were wearing their station uniforms, not fire-fighting uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time I will ask Ms. Stewart to please play another video-clip. It is 65 ter 22481C.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "On a night when half the city seems to be burning, they find out first hand what it's like to battle fires while dodging Serbian bullets. The gun-fire was coming from behind us and the fire was in front of us, so we were trying to hide and it really wasn't working out. "Get down, get down."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, are you in this video?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you respond to this fire?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I believe this fire was in October of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did this fire take place?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Near the -- near the Miljacka river at the juncture of the Grbavica salient and Skenderija.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the building. What type of building was it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: It was an industrial building. We were told at the time that it might have been a furniture factory, and there was a lot of wood and furniture in it which is why it burned like it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there anyone inside the building when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No. It was not a residential structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I could ask Ms. Stewart to please go back to 19 seconds into the video and pause the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I see it's a little bit blurred. If we could go forward just a second. Mr. Jordan, if you could look at the image before you, it is paused at 20 seconds. Do you recognise who is the person depicted at this point in the video?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After the initial comments by a news broadcaster, there was a voice that stated: "There was gun-fire that was coming from behind us and the fire was in front of us." Who was that person speaking and providing that description?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 31, you state: "The vast majority of fires I attended were in strictly civilian buildings." Between 1992 and 1995, how many times did you respond to a location of a fire that was a military target?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I think there were in the neighbourhood of a half-dozen occasions where we responded and found the burning structure to be strictly military, at which point we would leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Point of clarification, Your Honour. I believe learned counsel is talking about paragraph 30 of that statement rather than paragraph 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weber, we had difficulties in finding your quote in 31. So, thank you, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there occasions where you responded to a fire and found women and children inside the building?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The majority of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 27, you state: "By far, the vast majority of the victims were civilians going about their daily lives, trying to get food, trying to get water." How often did you see civilians being shot at on the streets of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: On a daily basis, other than certain lulls that occurred, but it was like that all the time. That was just daily life there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, I will ask Ms. Stewart to please play another video-clip under 65 ter 22481B, as in Boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "I'm sorry, there's 350,000 people living in Sarajevo going about their business every day and then getting bombed and shelled doing it."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you the person speaking in this video?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you provide this interview?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That interview was conducted at my home on, I believe, March 19th in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this video, there were people walking down a street. Do you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: It's an east/west road we used to take. We used to walk from the fire house on Skenderija to PTT, UN headquarters, on a regular basis, and that would be the high road that goes up behind the Holiday Inn. The picture depicts looking east.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: While you were in Sarajevo, did you see civilians reacting to gun-fire in a manner similar to those depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Stewart please play video-clip 65 ter 22481D, as in David.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: "Yes. We received a call at about 4.30 local time from the Holiday Inn saying that they have been impacted by a number of either rocket-propelled grenades or mortars. The Holiday Inn was shaken and then there was a fire reported. We responded with two fire engines and an ambulance and arrived here and almost immediately started taking heavy sniper fire directed at us. That's -- suspended the operation and the local brigade showed up about the same time. Between the two of us, we were able to extinguish the fire pretty much. However, we are taking heavy sniper fire at the time."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the voice of the person speaking in the video?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes. That would be Mark Anderson, deputy chief at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did this fire occur at the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I believe this one was in the fall of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There are a few vehicles depicted in this video. The first one was a truck with UN GOFRS in black lettering. Could you please tell us what this truck was.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That was our fire truck, a -- a pumper truck with a thousand gallons of water on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There was another white vehicle with blue sirens.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be our armoured ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who are the fire-fighters depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Fire-fighter Mark Partello of Newport, Rhode Island is seen at the front of truck. He was under fire at the time. The gentleman moving about was Trevor Gibson. He was not a fire-fighter. He was a police officer from London that served with us. He would be our liaison with the local cops and firemen. In that video, Trevor was subsequently shot by a ricochet right after the video ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 22481A through D into evidence as public exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection from the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 224 -- 2241A [sic] becomes Exhibit P132, Your Honours. Document 22481C becomes Exhibit P133, Your Honour. Document 22481B becomes Exhibit P134, Your Honours. Document 22481D becomes Exhibit P135, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are all admitted into evidence although the record shows a wrong -- you may have misspoken, Madam Registrar. The first one was 22481A. It has been corrected but I think it reflected what you said. All four are admitted as public exhibits. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I, just for the sake of the record, ask you to repeat, Mr. Jordan, one of the last remarks. On page 45, line 8, the last sentence is recorded as in that video Trevor was shot, but I heard that you said something different from that. Could you please repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Trevor was hit by a ricochet. A bullet came off the ground and hit him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was that to be seen in the video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It happened only moments after that footage ended, sir. But it was at that fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That is what I heard you telling us earlier. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 15 of your statement, you describe a process you followed when responding to a fire with local fire-fighters in Sarajevo. You indicate that you provided grid references when you were fired upon to the UN. When did you begin this procedure?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That procedure started in September 1993, after the UN signed the protection order for firemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you determine the location where the shooting or shelling was coming from in order to provide grid references?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Visual observation. We carried binoculars and night-vision gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were the grid references from which the firing -- the fire was coming located on Bosnian Serb army territory, or Bosnian government territory, or both?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I think all our reports wound up being on BSA territory. We were only engaged a couple of times from BiH territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraphs 19 and 20 of your statement, you describe two occasions where you were shot. In paragraph 19, you describe being hit in the chest with a bullet in November 1994, and you state: "We were fighting a fire at the time, right at the front -- front line, just north of Grbavica in Hero's Square." You continue to state: "I'm sure that the shot came from the Serb area of Grbavica." How is it that you are sure the shot came from Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The structures we were fighting the fire in were residential but they had civilians on the inside facing the city and troops on the outside facing south, up towards the high ground. We had to stretch hose from one structure to another and, at that point, I was exposed to open ground that went uphill, and there was nothing between me and where the shot came from above me. It wasn't all that far away, and the way it hit me, it drove me straight into the ground, and I heard the shot from above and was looking in that direction but didn't see any muzzle flash or anything like that. It was -- I exposed myself for a moment and took a bullet for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've mentioned troops. Were there any Bosnian government troops in the area; and, if so, how are you able to rule out the possibility that the shot came from those forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: At the time I was in the open stretching a hose, the hose did have to cross a trench, but the troops were all under cover. I don't think there were any within 50 feet of me, and it was one well-aimed shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you carrying a weapon on either of the occasions you were shot in 1993 or 1994?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, may I ask you one clarifying question: Whether you explained where the shot came from, do I understand you well that you were fighting the fire at such a short distance from the confrontation line that the fire coming from where you felt it came, that there was not much BiH territory left and it was so close to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was nothing but open ground between me and where the shot came from. There was nobody --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the closest structures from there were on the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraphs 22 and 40, you mention your contacts with Major Indic. In paragraph 40, you state: "Most of my dealings with the Serb forces were with Major Indic and with Serb fire-fighters." How often did you have contact with Major Indic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I saw Major Indic on a -- several times a week, up until the BSA took his liaison office out of the PTT. I would not always see him for business, but I would see him when I was in PTT, and any dealings I had referenced bringing equipment to Bosnian Serb firemen or visiting Pale, all those meetings began with liaisoning with Major Indic first. So he was my first point of contact on any dealings with the BSA side or bringing equipment into Sarajevo itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When approximately was it that Major Indic took his liaison office out of the PTT?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I don't know exactly -- I don't remember exactly when the office left there. I know he was there up until December of 1993. So I would have to say after Christmas of 1993, some point the BSA forces no longer maintained a liaison office right in PTT.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 14106. Mr. Jordan, while this is coming up, in paragraph 13, you comment on this "Washington Post" clipping from 21 December 1993 and state: "That was about a building which collapsed from shelling, and we called Major Indic in Lukavica to have the shelling stopped while we extracted a child trapped in the collapsed building. He would get the shelling stopped, and it did stop very soon thereafter." Were you part of the GOFRS team that responded to this collapsed building?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, I was the incident commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where was this building located?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Just north and slightly east of PTT. Within sight of the PTT building residential area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was inside the building when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: We were told three children were trapped in the building. There were numerous civilians going through the rubble, and there was us and a number of local firemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long after Major Indic was contacted did the shelling stop?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Within minutes. It was very prompt. The shelling was going on. When we arrived, there was still shelling. And we were informed the children were trapped. And via UNHCR and PTT, we contacted Major Indic, and I assured him there was no military activity going on where we were, and the shelling stopped in moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 12 of your statement, with respect to the DVD you provided, you state: "There are videos of the Sarajevo Fire Brigade and GOFRS in action. It includes a mother and son sniping incident in November 1994, during which the son was killed and the mother wounded. I wasn't physically present at the scene but some of my personnel were there." You then state the names of three members of GOFRS who were at the site. How did you learn about the sniping involving the mother and son in November 1994?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Deputy Chief Mark Anderson contacted me in our office in Washington and let me know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this on the same day or a different day than the day the boy was shot?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I believe he called me as soon as he got back to the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with Todd Bayly about what happened when the mother and boy were shot?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did this conversation occur?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: When I gave my initial statement in August of 2006 - was it? - excuse me. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Todd Bayly told you this -- did you have a conversation with Todd Bayly in 1994 about this incident, or did you only have a conversation with Todd Bayly about this incident in 2006?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: It was 2006 that I called Todd for some clarification about the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to what you knew in 1994, what were you told about what happened the day the mother and boy were shot?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The mother and child had just visited the fire truck and our personnel. It was a very active sniping day, so our personnel were pre-positioned where people were being shot. It was not their first response of the day but it affected them. The child had been asking for candy, which the firemen used to give out, and right after doing so, him and his mother were hit by a single bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart to please play another video-clip. It is 65 ter 22481E. The Prosecution does want to note for the record that there are graphic images of the victim of a sniping incident in this video. The Prosecution has notified the victim's family that this video would be played today, and we also wanted to alert the public to the fact that there are graphic images of the boy in the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, your previous question, was that about Scheduled Incident about F12.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we have adjudicated facts on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are aware of that. What's the use, if apparently on the basis of more direct evidence this has been established by a previous Trial Chamber, to ask the witness what he heard from others, not being a personal observer of what happened. So I'm a bit puzzled by that, also in view of the way in which you use your time in court. Mr. Jordan, this has got nothing to do with you. It's just a matter of procedural rules.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, worries, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course I'm mindful of the two adjudicated facts with respect to the incident. I have not gone into certain other details that he knows, and I was just trying to make it clear what the foundation was for the witness, for his knowledge of this. And I will, of course, be mindful of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please proceed, and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Go back. Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa! "BSA ... "She is hurt. "Right now -- you're on his hands. In the unit. In the unit. In the unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, in the video, did you recognise the intersection where the boy was laying?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where that's located?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That's the zebra crossing on the 6th Proletariat Brigade Boulevard right by the museum.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the names of the GOFRS fire-fighters who are in this video.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The first person you see is deputy chief Mark Anderson from Washington. Then there is Trevor Gibson from Scotland, Todd Bayly from Canada, and Josh Wooding from Kansas. And Randy Holliman [phoen] from Nevada.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the video, the boy was turned over and then placed into an ambulance. Do you recognise this ambulance?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes. That was our former military ambulance that we got from excess stocks in Europe. It was unarmoured. The first ambulance in the video was our armoured ambulance, and the last one was our semi-armoured Volkswagen ambulance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you to clarify so the record is clear: Which ambulance was the boy placed into?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The unarmoured one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: A woman and a young girl were placed into a different vehicle. Could you please tell us what vehicle that was?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be a Volkswagen van that we had kind of self-armoured on the inside ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I please have just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders the video-clip 65 ter 22481E into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 22481E becomes Exhibit P136, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P136 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, what do you plan to do with 14106?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you for catching that, Your Honour. I see I missed that. I was going to leave it as a housekeeping item to tender at the end of the examination. I forgot to do so at the time. With the Chamber's leave, I would tender 65 ter 14106 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Also no objection. That's one of the ones we had discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14106 becomes Exhibit P137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, in paragraph 29 of your statement, you state: "From my visits to the Serb side, I could see mortar tubes well dug in with their triangulation equipment and aiming stakes out. There's no doubt they were fixed positions with covers and corridors set up, and there was no doubt they knew what they were aiming at." Where did you see these mortars?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: When we would visit the Serb environment in Grbavica, we would have to go around the mountain via the airport, Lukavica, then up the back side and down into Lukavica. So the ridge line above Sarajevo to the south was where many BSA gun positions were. So we passed them on a regular basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately on how many occasions did you go to Lukavica and then continue down along the ridge line to the south of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I'm sure we did that trip near a dozen times in the -- in the three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, the Prosecution tenders the witness. No further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you, Mr. Weber. Mr. Ivetic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour, and I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just wondering, we'll take a break in six minutes from now. If you could choose a subject matter which you could conclude within the next six minutes, then that would be appreciated. Mr. Jordan, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, at the beginning, first of all, good day. I have some questions that I would like to ask you to try and clarify portions of your testimony and to get a better understanding of them. As was case with Mr. Weber, since we both speak the English language, I would caution you to try and observe a pause between my question and your answer, and I shall try to do likewise.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to first discuss a topic that you've just mentioned from paragraph 29 of your statement. You talked about mortar positions that you observed. Am I correct that you never eye-witnessed these mortar positions while they were firing?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No, sir. Not when I was observing them in passing them. I did see them fire when I was down in the city but never when I was in proximity to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, first I'd-like to go through some questions with respect to your background. The statement that is dated 2006 that was tendered into evidence lists your current employment as director of the NGO, Global Operation Fire Rescue Services. Is that still the case?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your current employment is.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I work in construction right now. I do residential home renovations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Can you tell us when is the last date that you were affiliated as the director of the NGO, Global Operation Fire Rescue Services, which I will now call GOFRS for the remainder of my questioning?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: We shut down GOFRS in 2001, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Up until 2001, during the existence of the NGO GOFRS, do you have any approximation as for your annual budget and where you obtained your financing from?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: After 1995, GOFRS basically existed only on paper and with funding I myself put into it. We put in our own money, myself and a few of our remaining personnel. I travelled to several places to explore deployments between working in construction, and those deployments never worked out, and we decided to shut things down in 2001 with the events of 9/11. So GOFRS as a unit never really deployed after Bosnia. We did try to keep it going. We failed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic -- Just for my understanding, so when we read on the cover page of your 2006 statement: Current occupation director of GOFRS, that it was already outdated. Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when in paragraph 2 I read: "I am the founder and director of," then it, I should understand that to be I was the founder -- I am the founder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I was the director of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just one question before the break. I believe we're up against that time. Sir, during the time period that GOFRS was in existence, did GOFRS do any consultancy with the work with the government organs of the United States or any state or local government of any state at any level?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: We were asks to go to Haiti by the US army, which we did, and spent some time there looking at getting their fire department back on its feet. But in spite of the army's invitation, the State Department decided to go another route. We were a NGO. It wound up being contracted out.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we are at the time reference that you'd indicated you'd wish to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could Mr. Jordan be escorted out. We'd like to see you back in 25 minutes, Mr. Jordan. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Ivetic, could you give us any indication about the time you'd need in cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I'd indicated to the Office of the Prosecutor that I anticipated one hour and 30 to 40 minutes for this witness in total. I believe I'm still on that estimate, so I should be somewhere between 1 hour and 20 minutes to 1 hour and 30 minutes, and so I believe we used about 12 minutes during the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's granted, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, before the break, we talked about GOFRS, the NGO. Now I would like to ask you some questions about yourself personally, and I'll ask you a similar question to the last question that we had. Did you personally do any consultancy with any government organs of the United States at a state or local government thereof at any level?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: As a paid consultant, no. I worked as a NGO. I have lectured at the US Naval War College and at the Marine Corps war fighting laboratory in Quantico, Virginia, and from time to time have been an instructor in military subjects overseas, but that was not to do with GOFRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, I think your answer was about 90 per cent clear. Has none of this consultancy work ever had any anything to do with fire-fighting or emergency services while fire-fighting?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Well, yes. The lecture series with the marine corps and the navy was about conducting fire-fighting and rescue operations in hostile environments. Also, the marine corps was more focussed on counter-sniping, so I talked to them about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With regard to the time-period that you spent in the United States Marine Corps, did you have occasion to see active combat as a marine?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No, sir. Not as a marine.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You qualify your answer. Apart from the experience in Sarajevo, did you have occasion to see active combat in the course of your experiences?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Could you tell us what other instances apart from the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the 1990s wherein you saw active combat?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I spent some time in Beirut. I spent some time in Central America. I lived in the Congo mostly working as a medic. So, yes, I've seen some combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And I apologise. I'm not dissatisfied with your answer, I just am waiting for the transcript to catch up with us. What was the highest rank that you obtained within the marine corps?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be sergeant, E-5.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As an E-5 sergeant, how many men at arms did you have under your command?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: At one time I was a platoon sergeant in a weapons platoon, which gave me approximately 40 men. My last job was as a chief scout sniper in a -- what was called a STANO platoon, meaning Surveillance, Target, Acquisition and Night Operations. That gave me about 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, until now, the Chamber is puzzled about relevance of these details, but make that clear as soon as you can, because you're supposed to present relevant evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe that the background of the witness and his training is relevant, as is his knowledge of persons on the ground of that reputation, and we're getting to that section, Your Honours, so I would ask the Court's indulgence. And if I do ask any question that Your Honours believe is improper under the Rules, I would ask that I be advised of that and I will consider that at that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Come to your point as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, where -- wherein you were posted as a marine, did you have occasion to become engaged in any clandestine operations or activities outside of the United States? And for purposes of this question, sir, if feel that you can't answer this question, I understand, and you can tell me so.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I'm not going to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to have to repeat what Judge Orie had asked just a few minutes ago, and I'm going to ask the question very pointedly: Is that purpose of that question intended to say -- to -- to go to the credibility of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In part it does, Your Honour. Depending on the answers. I obviously don't know 100 per cent all the answers to the questions that I ask, but I have an idea based upon the information that has been provided for this witness. It also goes to his training and to methods in -- which were employed on the ground and whether those methods that were employed were of a strictly military nature or of a strictly fire-fighting nature, and I believe it's is necessary to understand in particular the evidence of this witness as to incoming fire that came towards him and his colleagues to understand the training and the manner of operation that they had on the ground, because those are items that are, I believe, relevant to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ivetic, to the extent that I listened here to the witness, he was in Sarajevo as a fire-fighter and he's testified about things that he observed while he was fire-fighting fire. He's not talking about his expertise as a fire-fighter. He is telling us what he saw happen on the ground. So he comes across to me as a fact witness, not an expert witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree that is he a fact witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Ivetic, all the things you say you would like to know from the witness, ask him about that, more directly. Go more straighter to where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They're not even [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But they're not even relevant to his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I beg to differ. The statement of the witness talks about the witness as a fire-fighter shooting upon persons. I don't know if Your Honours are familiar with that. But I believe, therefore that it is very much relevant what his military training was, what his standard procedures and protocols were for operations. Those are directly relevant to the testimony in his statement which has entered under Rule 92 ter and which I have to therefore address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it make any difference whether he had once 20 or 80 people under his command? These kind of details. If that's what you want to know, ask the witness about it in a more direct way so that we come to the point as quickly as possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't believe I have a pending question, so I will move on the next question, sir, and I will be as direct as possible in trying to further the comments -- to comply with the comments of the Chamber. Sir, am I correct that in the course of your work with the marine corps you were also part of an intelligence battalion, the rifle battalion intelligence?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, the scout sniper platoon is in the table of organisation equipment in the S2, intelligence section. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I have to ask you this with regard to your deployment to Sarajevo, the DVD that you provided to the Office of the Prosecutor, among the items there is a speech by Vice-President Al Gore of the United States praising you for taking up President Clinton's call to intervene in Bosnia. Did you go to Bosnia at the behest of the United States government in any capacity?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: No, sir. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With regard to the time-period when you left the marines, am I correct, sir, and I think this is at paragraph 2 of your statement, that you were a marksmanship instructor in many different nations. Can we clarify if this was as a marine or as a private citizen?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That was a private citizen, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you at that time what is considered a paid mercenary or independent contract -- private contractor?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I was an advisor and instructor. I was not a paid soldier of a country other than the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I want to clarify one thing and I'm going to show what's been marked as Prosecution 65 ter number 14104, and this is a one-page article. And in the middle of that article, there is a curious reference about you. First of all, am I correct that this article is from the time-period that you were -- one of the time-periods that you went to Bosnia-Herzegovina and to Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the middle of this article, and I quote now. It says: "Both point Comenisoli [phoen] and Allen point to Jordan, a ten-year marine veteran, as the driving force behind providing fire-fighters with much needed supplies." And the question I have for you, sir, is very simple: How do you account for the fact that this publication of the Department of Defence lists you as a ten-year marine veteran when, in fact, your testimony is that you only were a five-year marine veteran?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I would have to put that in the same category as the one article that describes me as being from Harrison, New York, and I have never been to Harrison, New York. The media often gets things, whether civilian or military, incorrect. I don't know why they came up with ten, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. And the media in this case, this is Stars and Stripes magazine. This is the Department of Defence authorised daily newspaper; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes. It is my understanding that the article was written by what looks like senior airman, that would be an enlisted man.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to turn to your first trip to Sarajevo or Bosnia-Herzegovina. Am I correct that as part of your first deployment in 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would just inquire as to whether or not the Defence intends to tender the article. We would not object to it, but we would be then seeking to enter it ourselves for context.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, what I -- the evidence of the witness is that what was published here, you've his attention only to being described as a ten-year marine veteran, that he says that's factually wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I explained that is what I was asking the question about and he's clarified that. I don't see a reason to introduce it as part of my evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we leave it as it is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with regard to your first deployment, I believe that was in November of 1992, am I correct that this was not co-ordinated by -- with the United Nations but, rather, was co-ordinated by you via the Bosnian Embassy?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would I be -- also be correct that during this first trip, this was before the NGO had been created and that you travelled alone in the capacity of a private citizen?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that at the time of your first trip to Sarajevo in November 1992, sir, you had only served as a volunteer fireman in the state of Rhode Island for approximately six months?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be correct, sir, in addition to some experience fighting wild fires in the American west.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to your deployment to Sarajevo, did you obtain any briefing or training as to the parties on the ground and as to any assessment as to how the war or conflict started in that region?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I received minimal information from the Bosnian Embassy. At the time, I only knew what I had gleaned from magazine articles and the graphic footage we saw of the firemen and what they were going through. So I did not know nearly what I should have known before I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, both and you and have I used the term "Bosnian Embassy." Am I correct that when you use that term you imply the forces that were allied with Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At the time that you went to Sarajevo in November of 1992, did people in Sarajevo - that is to say, on both sides of the conflict line - know of your background previously serving as a US marine?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I know I spoke to the Bosnian Embassy about that, that I had served in the marines. I found them to be more interested in the fire-fighting aspect, not my former military service, and found that to be also true of the firemen that I was with when I first got to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to now ask you the same question. Did persons -- on a different aspect. Did persons in Sarajevo both -- on both sides of the conflict line become aware of your prior history as a paid private contractor for several nations training armed forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I would say yes, because the military situation in Sarajevo, in and around Sarajevo, completely overshadowed the fire and rescue operations we were trying to conduct, and one of the first things I realised, which, I think, anyone, ex-marine or not, would realise, that the fire departments needed on both sides, was protection, which the UN was not, at the time, providing, so the firemen could do their jobs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordan, could I invite you to directly answer the question. The question was whether, in Sarajevo, people on both sides of the conflict line became aware of your prior history? Did you tell them? Did they show in any way that they were aware?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My military background came out, sir, as a result of all the military activity around us. When you are fighting a fire in residential structures where sometimes people hide weapons in walls, it became clear that I knew how to handle them and put them in a safe condition so we could continue fighting fires. Also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you can gain a lot of military experience without anyone knowing that you had been contracted as a private person for several nations training armed forces. That's -- the two are not the same. You are talking about military experience. The question was about anyone being aware of your past, being engaged in contracting in military training for other nations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sure some people were aware of it. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had people ask me because I -- you run into some of the same people in the course of international operations, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told to some of them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If somebody asked me, Were you doing such-and-such, I'd say, Yes. I had no reason to lie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you just raised an interesting point while answering Judge Orie's question. You indicated that while fighting fires in residential structures you often would come across weapons hidden in the walls. Am I correct that you are talking about residential structures within the territory of the ABiH forces in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Prior to going to Sarajevo, had you attended any formal educational forces in fire safety or relating to the work of fire-fighting or obtained any degrees from any such institution?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I passed the basic fire-fighters course in Bristol, Rhode Island, enough to earn my badge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir. If we can now move to some specific points I would like to address. In paragraph 7 of your statement -- I apologise, sir. Do you have a copy in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Not at this time, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have the -- it's Exhibit P126. If we can have that pulled up in e-court, and I'm focussing on the second page in the English. Paragraph number 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would it be helpful if the witness would have a hard copy as well so that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It would, Your Honour, and I would defer to opposing counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that the Prosecution has a copy available. Do you want to inspect it, Mr. Ivetic, or do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do not. If Mr. Weber says it's clean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it can be given to the witness right away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I can draw your attention to paragraph 7. In your statement you state that: "The first month or so I worked on making sure that the fuel which the UN was donating to the local fire department was actually being given by the Bosnian government to the local fire department." My question for you, sir: Can we take from this statement that you had knowledge of instances where persons in the Bosnian government were misappropriating humanitarian aid and using it for purposes other than which they were intended?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I know that fuel meant for the fire department was not getting to the fire department until there was international oversight. There was none till we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when say again the Bosnian government, are we again talking about the government that was led by Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 8 of your statement, this -- here you mention and you state that quote/unquote: "We decided to form the NGO." If you could just briefly, you don't have to give names, but by giving us an idea of who the other person are that were affiliated with you when you formed the NGO?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be my partner at the time, Elizabeth Hoban, and four buddies from work. We decided we were going to address the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to talk about your subsequent engagements in Sarajevo. We previously saw the article about -- from Stars and Stripes that was about a military plane that brought some equipment in. Am I correct, sir, that when you went back to Sarajevo, at one point you could not arrange a means of getting your gear into Sarajevo and you had to arrange an unofficial US military transport plane?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I'm not aware that there any unofficial military transport planes. We basically secured the support of a senator back home, Senator Pell, who made a phone call and got space for us on military transport to get equipment from the States to Frankfurt. Once in Frankfurt, we were able to get in line with the rest of the UN air-lift aircraft to get equipment into Sarajevo. While those aircraft may have been US, they were tasked to the UN. So the only strictly US military aircraft we ever got access to was from the states to Europe. After that, it was all UN, whose ever colours they happened to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic I would like to ask a follow-up question to the witness. You said your partner at the time, and then you gave her name. Now, the family name of your partner at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hoban, sir. H-O-B-A-N.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that makes my question superfluous. It was wrongly spelled. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Orie.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you Prosecution 65 ter number 14094. And while we wait for that, I can tell you that this is another of the articles that you provided to the Prosecution, and it is a Firehouse magazine article dated sometime in 1994. Do you recall this as one of the articles that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I direct your attention to the first column of this article, and it's at the bottom of the first column and runs off to the top of the middle column, and the selection says quote, talking about you, I believe: "He adds that Sarajevo has its own city ambulances but because of local corruption, most are used as taxis by local politicians and don't pick up patients." Sir, does this article accurately reflect a comment that you made to Firehouse magazine in or about 1994.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, again, is this section talking about local politicians, would that be talking about local politicians belonging to the government of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One other question I have to ask about this article, and this comes from the last or third column. It's in the middle of that, and I will -- I'll read it for you and hopefully the -- the English version will reflect that. There it is. "Not only does the GOFRS team in Sarajevo provide fire and EMS support for the UN and local civilians, they also are called upon to serve as the EMS team when US politicians visit the area. In one instance, they were requested to provide temporary security for the US Embassy in Sarajevo because the state department's diplomatic security unit couldn't make it into Sarajevo on time." And, sir, again, does this article accurately reflect information that you provided to the Firehouse magazine in 1994?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I to understand from this section that you and your team served as armed guards for the US Embassy at some point in time in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How many of your men served with you as armed guards for the US Embassy?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The statement reflects, I think -- I think it was less than maybe two or three incidents where the embassy, again like it says, could not get people in due to flights being cancelled. They asked us to just stand by until security did. The vast majority of my personnel did not carry weapons. Only a few who had either police or military experience did. This was partially a result of the UN's not wanting to provide assistance to the embassy. The common phrase among UNPROFOR was that if the Americans need more security, they can send some US troops. I completely saw their point. We also helped other embassies, but, of course, would not say no to our own if they asked us for any assistance that we thought was legitimate to provide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "we" and "my people," are you talking about fellow members of the GOFRS fire-fighting service that served as armed guards for the US and other embassies on several other occasions?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes. And only -- again, only the personnel who were trained to handle weapons and were willing to do so, did. We did not require everybody to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If I can then move on. Who provided the weaponry used in this task of securing the US and other embassies on several occasions in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: We brought our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see that the exhibit -- the document is still up on the screen. I would inquire of the Prosecution if there's an objection or if I can tender this as an exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 14094 becomes Exhibit D41, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D41 is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated you brought your own weapons. Can I ask you, sir, how it was that you brought these weapons into Sarajevo? And -- well, I'll leave it -- you can answer in way that is appropriate, sir.

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Well, they all passed through various customs in the US, Europe, and then we get on the plane. If we were flying in that day from Frankfurt or when we drove in sometimes we'd bring in convoys of equipment. Everything was out and in the open. Nothing was hidden.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can direct your attention to, I believe, it's paragraph 34 of your statement, and I think that details some of the weapons that you personally brought. Am I correct that you had a US M14 battle rifle and a Barrett sniper rifle, as well as a 50-calibre weapon?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The Barrett is a 50-calibre weapon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question, since I know it's known as the light 50. Thank you. What about the M14, is that a weapon that you also had on your person?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: The M1A version, civilian non-automatic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the reference to paragraph 34 accurate, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One, moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it doesn't give any details but you're now eliciting the details from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. I was trying to supplement the information that I know of about this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if we could just briefly talk about the M1 -- M14 variant. Am I correct that this is a -- albeit a semi-automatic, it's still a battle rifle; it fires a 7.62-millimetre bullet?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: That would be correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And during the time-period you were residing in Rhode Island; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was possession of both of these armaments in Rhode Island authorised by local law at the time in question?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that both of these weapons are in particular -- strike that. Would you agree with me that at least the Barrett sniper rifle is considered a military grade weapon?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the slug fired by this weapon is the 12.7 times 99 NATO bullet that is used in the Browning heavy machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. What about the other members of your team that were armed that were providing security for various embassies in Sarajevo? Did they also have what is called military grade armaments?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to your -- load out that you used -- pardon me, the ammunition, was that also military grade ammunition?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could focus now on your everyday activities with the GOFRS as a fire-fighting unit. Am I correct that it was a well known fact to everyone in the area on both sides of the conflict line that both yourself and albeit not all but several members of your team were armed and carried these military-grade weapons with you in the course of your duties?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That would be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question there. If you say carried these military-grade weapons with you, would you mean that you carried them with your body or that you had them in your vehicles? Because reading your statement, I got the impression that when you were having your weapons with you, that they were in the car but not necessarily in your hands.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be true, Your Honour. Most of the time we kept them in the vehicles, the long guns. The personnel who functioned as MLOs, military liaisons, they carried handguns which were, of course, on them, but there was very little walking around with a rifle on anybody's part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: On how many occasions would you estimate that you yourself actually had to draw one of your weapons and fire the same or threaten to do so during the entire time you were in Sarajevo while you were on duty as a fire-fighter? And when I say "in Sarajevo," I intend to include both sides of the conflict line?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: I don't think I ever threatened anybody with a rifle. It either came out and was used or did not come out at all. Scores of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to your colleagues in the GOFRS as to on how many occasions those that were armed took out their weapons and actually fired them at somebody in the course of providing fire-fighting services in Sarajevo, again, on both sides of the conflict line?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: It would be minimal from my personnel. I handled most of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we can look at -- I believe it's paragraph 23 of your statement. We've talked about several times when you were struck by snipers. Here in paragraph 23 is another incident that the Prosecution did not go into, but I would like to. Here you talk about an incident where you were wounded and your vehicle was, quote/unquote "ventilated." Now I understand what you mean, sir, but for those that do not know military jargon, what -- what do you mean -- by that do you mean that the mortar shrapnel penetrated your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: JOHN JORDAN
utterances.text: Yes. We were responding to a house fire. We had already stretched hoses from the truck down to the house on fire, and a number of mortar rounds then landed in close proximity to the trucks and filled the trucks full of holes, ventilated them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct, sir, you, sir, were wounded on this occasion, and this is the only time you were actually physically wounded?
